title: Painted Deserts Drone Post-Processing: Zone-Based RAW-to-Photoshop Workflow with Directional Lighting

date.basis: Embedded creation time provided in metadata (2022-10-18T21:53:33Z) and transcript references to an October Painted Deserts tour.

locations.name: Painted Deserts tour
locations.basis: Explicit mention in transcript: 'Think about these things. What we're going to talk about is how to process drone photographs from the Painted Deserts tour in October here.'

summary: This instructional video presents a practical, zone-based approach to post-processing drone imagery from the Painted Deserts tour. It emphasizes starting in RAW for global adjustments, then transferring to Photoshop for localized refinements using tools like the history brush, clone stamp, and selective color workflows. The instructor demonstrates building three zones in complex images, painting directional light to create depth, and applying techniques such as the Orton effect, perspective warp, and tonal-based color adjustments to enhance skies and landscapes, including drone panoramas.

sections.title: Intro and zone-based processing philosophy
sections.description: The presenter introduces the idea of identifying how many processing zones an image contains and why many drone shots (especially long-lens or abstract ones) benefit from a single-zone approach, with more complex scenes requiring multiple zones and targeted adjustments in Photoshop rather than raw.

sections.title: RAW-first, then Photoshop for localized edits
sections.description: Discussion of doing most processing in RAW at first, applying global changes, and reserving masking/adjustment brushes for Photoshop to target specific parts of the image when needed. The speaker demonstrates starting exposure low and using whites to pull back glow.

sections.title: Color grading philosophy and selective color vs HSL
sections.description: Explains tonal-based color adjustments and why selective color can be more refined than HSL for drone imagery. The presenter demonstrates subtle uses of color grading to push highlights and shadows toward desired hues and uses blue in camera calibration to influence the overall palette.

sections.title: Photoshop workflow and history-based non-destructive edits
sections.description: Demonstrates returning to RAW via the Camera Raw filter, leveraging the history brush with a high number of history states, and painting adjustments from previous steps to refine specific areas while preserving the ability to revert or revive past edits.

sections.title: Three-zone directional-light workflow on landscapes and abstracts
sections.description: Shows a workflow for multi-zone images (sky, midground, rocks/foreground) and how to build strong light sources by painting light with large and small brushes, applying diffusion for atmosphere, and guiding the eye toward the light source.

sections.title: Wider shots, rule of trapezoids, and sky expansion
sections.description: Addresses widening shots using perspective warp and the rule of trapezoids to extend the frame, as well as sky expansion techniques to create more sky area while maintaining a natural look. The section also notes alternatives like fisheye distortion and distortion/scaling in RAW.

sections.title: Tonal-based color adjustments for skies and focal-point sun
sections.description: Details tonal-based approaches to color the sky after widening, then building a sun focal point by layering glow, luminosity, and selective color adjustments. Emphasizes painting light into skies and foregrounds to create a convincing sunrise/sunset feel.

sections.title: Panorama processing, cloning, focus stacking, and wrap-up
sections.description: Covers drone panorama workflows, cloning between images to refine reflections and edges, and focus-stacking considerations. The speaker compares history-based painting with clone-paint for controlling edits, and briefly touches on merging multiple shots in Photoshop.
